title: pvLoopSubdivision
body:
## pvLoopSubdivision

Refines a triangle surface with Loop's approximating subdivision: each pass splits every triangle into four and repositions points so the surface becomes smooth; point data are interpolated by the same scheme and new triangles inherit their parent's cell data. Use it to smooth coarse triangulated geometry for display. Input must be polydata of triangles only (run triangulate first). Because points move, the result no longer passes through the original vertices; use pvSubdivide for refinement that keeps the shape.

Common mistakes and assumptions:

- Each pass quadruples the triangle count; NumberofSubdivisions 4 gives 256 times as many triangles.
- Do not measure areas or volumes on the smoothed surface as if it were the original geometry.
- Schemaxis generates this binding from ParaView's catalogue; it has not run a native acceptance check for this operation.

Native constructor: `LoopSubdivision`. Identity: `filters/LoopSubdivisionFilter`. Role: `pipeline`. Output kinds: `["data"]`.

ParaView: This property specifies the input to the Loop Subdivision filter. Accepted data: polygonal data (surfaces, lines or vertices) (vtkPolyData). | True | one object | `data` | `{"compatibility":"native-domain-checked","composite":null,"cost":{"basis":"no benchmark","conversion":"none inserted","rating":"unknown"},"nativeTypes":["vtkPolyData"],"requirements":{},"traits":{"contiguity":"unknown","indexing":"unknown","iteration":"unknown"}}` |

| Key | Meaning / native assignment | Type and constraints | Default / required | Example value |
